MINUTES
  MALIBU PLANNING COMMISSION
  REGULAR MEETING
  JUNE 6, 2022
  TELECONFERENCED VARIOUS LOCATIONS
  -

  6:30 P.M.

The following meeting was held pursuant to the Governor’s Executive Orders N-25-20
and N-29-20 and fully teleconferenced from various locations during the coronavirus
disease (COVID-19) pandemic.

CALL TO ORDER

  Chair Hill called the meeting to order at 6:31 p.m.

ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance by the Recording Secretary:

  PRESENT: Chair Kraig Hill, Vice Chair Dennis Robert Smith, and Commissioners Jeffrey
  D. Jennings, John G. Mazza, and Mark Wetton

  ALSO PRESENT: Richard Mollica, Planning Director; Adrian Fernandez, Assistant
  Planning Director; Trevor Rusin, Assistant City Attorney; Philip Coronel, Assistant
  Planner; Jessica Thompson, Senior Planner; Lauren Doyel, Coastal Engineer and
  Geotechnical Reviewer; and Rebecca Evans, Recording Secretary

APPROVAL OF AGENDA

MOTION  Commissioner Mazza moved and Commissioner Jennings seconded a motion to
  approve the agenda as recommended by staff, with Item Nos. 5.D. and 5.E.
  continued to the June 20, 2022 Regular Planning Commission meeting.

  The question was called and the motion carried unanimously.

REPORT ON POSTING OF AGENDA

  Recording Secretary Evans reported that the agenda for the meeting was properly
  posted on May 27, 2022.

ITEM 1  CEREMONIAL/PRESENTATIONS
  None.

ITEM 2.A.  PUBLIC COMMENTS

  Lonnie Gordon, Rosemarie Ihde, Cohn Drummond, Rosemary Sampson donated
  one minute per person to Jo Drummond for a total of seven minutes.

  Pat Healy confirmed that Item No. 5.E. was removed from the meeting agenda.

  Jo Drummond asserted that Administrative Plan Reviews had been improperly
  granted. She requested that the City cure and correct administrative errors and
  demanded permit revocation hearings for several Administrative Plan Review
  Woolsey Fire projects. Ms. Drummond asked for different treatment for proposed
  developments based on ownership. She questioned whether the term existing could
  be applied to a fire-destroyed home based on Section 13.4.6 of the LIP.

  Scott Dittrich expressed concern regarding the City’s legal liability based on Jo
  Drummond’s claims. He questioned why the wireless tower did not come before
  the Public Works Commission. Mr. Dittrich urged the Planning Commission to
  agendize the item and direct staff to order the removal of the current tower.

  Ryan Embree stated the Civic Center wireless tower was not a like-kind
  replacement for the previous tower and noted differences in massing and view
  permeability.

  Bill Sampson seconded Jo Drummond’s statements. He stated he would like the
  wireless antenna torn down and commended the Planning Commission on their
  work towards Morning View traffic control.

ITEM 2.B.  COMMISSION I STAFF COMMENTS

  Commissioner Wetton noted that the issues raised during public comment were
  addressed in prior meetings with responses already provided by staff.

  Commissioner Mazza requested that the Planning Department provide a progress
  report regarding the wireless tower and contact with the Federal Aviation
  Administration regarding paint colors.

  In response to Commissioner Mazza, Planning Director Molhica stated he spoke
  with the project manager for the wireless tower and asked about changing the paint
  color. The Santa Monica College District had not yet responded; however, they had
  completed a public records request for all documents related to the Malibu public
  hearing on the project.
   Malibu Planning Commission
  Minutes of June 6, 2022
  Page 3 ofl2

 Chair Hill requested clarification from Planning Director Mollica on the view
 permeability of the original wireless tower and whether it was for emergency use
 only, in comparison to the current tower that would be rented to third parties.

In response to Chair Hill, Planning Director Mollica stated that a memorandum
with the status of the wireless tower was posted on the City of Malibu Planning
Department website along with links for further information. He agreed that the
current tower was a different type. However, the previous tower also leased space
to a wireless telecommunications carrier.

Chair Hill stated Ms. Drummond asserted that the code had not been followed for
any of the projects over ten percent and asked Planning Director Mollica to respond.

Planning Director Mollica explained that the City did receive a letter from the
California Coastal Commission (CCC) and the City had been reviewing their
statements. There was not an exact definition of the term existing in the code. The
City was looking into the issues raised by the CCC and had notified City Council.
Out of an abundance of caution, option four was removed from the City’s website
as a precautionary measure while the issue was investigated. All pending approvals
which did not have a decision issued had been put on hold.

 Commissioner Jennings expressed that there was a fundamental mistake made
 during public comment. Not all the Administrative Plan Review approvals issued
 to fire victims would have required a full Coastal Development Permit and hearing.
 He understood Ms. Drummond to believe that the planning verification plus ten
percent residence would need to be built with a certificate of occupancy issued prior
to application for a remodel, which would be stunningly inefficient. When the CCC
delivered the approved Local Coastal Program and Local Implementation Plan to
the City, they stated that it was up to the City to interpret and apply the documents
These projects were outside of the CCC appeal zones and their agency’s opinion
should not have carried much weight. Hundreds of people, including the
Commissioner himself, had spent thousands of dollars following the process
provided by the City of Malibu. Those concerned with the potential for legal action
should be most concerned about the likelihood of lawsuits from those who followed
the system the City outlined whose time and money may have been wasted. He
noted that the upcoming election season was likely to continue to generate rhetoric.

Commissioner Mazza stated that the City followed a serial development policy in
the past. The Business Roundtable report included a statement that the June Hotel
was now operating with a swimming pool and new landscaping.

In response to Commissioner Mazza, Planning Director Mollica confirmed that
June Hotel had a pending application which would be coming before the Planning
   Malibu Planning Commission
  Minutes of June 6, 2022
  Page 4 of 12

  Commission for review. They also had a small amount of permitted work which
  was authorized to repair smoke damage. That location did install landscaping
  without the benefit of permit which resulted in a code enforcement action. As part
  of that code enforcement action the landscaping had been cut back due to height in
  the front yard setback. Planning Director Mollica would continue to investigate any
  changes in their operations for code compliance.

  Commissioner Wetton stated he did not currently, nor had he ever been engaged in
  contract or public works projects. Commissioner Mazza seconded Commissioner
  Wetton’s comments.

  Chair Hill expressed a desire to move forward with a hybrid meeting model for
  future meetings. He mentioned Land Use Policy 1(A) discussed Environmentally
  Sensitive Habitat Areas as presumptive and listed several biomes in the City unless
  site specific evidence showed them not to play an important role. The evidentiary
  burden appeared to be opposite that applied by the City Biologist.

  Commissioner Jennings noted the CCC provided designated ESHA maps but did
  not have the staffing to review each site in the City and therefore relied on the City’s
  site-specific evaluations.

  Planning Director Mollica announced the school district confirmed that they would
  remove the rearmost parking lot (lot F) from their plans and staff requested updated
  site plans from the school for the City Council hearing.
